title: Formal Writing
subtitle: Master letters, meeting reports, and synthesis notes

lessons.title: La lettre formelle
lessons.description: Learn the conventions, structure, and set formulas of formal French letters.

blocks.heading: The anatomy of a formal letter
blocks.body: A French formal letter follows a fixed layout: sender's address top left, recipient's address top right, place and date, a reference line (objet), the salutation, the body in clearly separated paragraphs, and a closing formula before the signature. Skipping any of these pieces reads as careless, even if the French inside is perfect.

examples.french: Objet : Demande de renseignements
examples.english: Subject: Request for information
examples.note: objet states the letter's purpose in a few words

examples.note: place then date, always this order

examples.french: Madame, Monsieur,
examples.english: Dear Sir or Madam,
examples.note: used when you don't know the recipient's name

blocks.tip: Never start a formal letter with 'Bonjour' — it is too casual for administrative or professional correspondence.

blocks.heading: Opening formulas
blocks.body: The salutation must match what you know about the recipient. Use the title alone (Madame, Monsieur) with no name if you are writing to an institution, and add the surname only if you know it and it is a modest hierarchy. Never use 'Cher/Chère' unless you already have a personal relationship with the recipient.

examples.english: Dear Sir or Madam,

examples.english: Dear Director,

blocks.heading: Closing formulas
blocks.body: French closing formulas are longer and more ceremonial than English ones. The classic pattern repeats the opening address inside the closing sentence. Shorter formulas like 'Cordialement' or 'Bien à vous' suit emails and less formal professional exchanges, not official administrative letters.

examples.french: Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
examples.english: Yours faithfully.
examples.note: the most formal closing, for administration

examples.french: Je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, l'expression de mes sentiments respectueux.
examples.english: Yours sincerely.

examples.french: Cordialement,
examples.english: Best regards,

blocks.tip: The closing formula must repeat the exact title used in the salutation — 'Madame' opens, 'Madame' closes.

blocks.heading: The polite conditional for requests
blocks.body: Formal letters almost never use the imperative or a blunt 'je veux'. Instead, the conditional softens requests into polite suggestions: 'je voudrais', 'je souhaiterais', 'pourriez-vous', 'il conviendrait de'. This distance between the verb form and the direct demand is exactly what marks a text as formal in French.

examples.french: Je souhaiterais obtenir des informations complémentaires.
examples.english: I would like to obtain further information.

examples.french: Pourriez-vous me confirmer la réception de ce courrier ?
examples.english: Could you confirm receipt of this letter?

examples.french: Il conviendrait de revoir les termes du contrat.
examples.english: It would be appropriate to review the terms of the contract.

blocks.tip: Stacking 'je vous serais reconnaissant(e) de bien vouloir + infinitive' is the most formal request pattern of all.

blocks.heading: Nominalization: turning verbs into nouns
blocks.body: Administrative and formal French favours nouns over verbs where everyday French would use a verb. 'Nous avons reçu votre demande' can become 'Accusé de réception de votre demande' as a heading. Learning to nominalize — verb to noun — is what makes a letter sound official rather than conversational.

passages.title: Une lettre de réclamation
passages.french:
Claire Dubreuil
14 rue des Lilas, 75011 Paris
Service Clientèle - Énergie Plus
8 avenue de la République, 69003 Lyon
Paris, le 5 février 2026
Objet : Réclamation concernant la facture n° 4521
Madame, Monsieur,
Je me permets de vous contacter au sujet de la facture n° 4521, reçue le 20 janvier dernier, dont le montant me semble erroné.
En effet, le tarif appliqué ne correspond pas à celui indiqué sur le devis que vous m'aviez transmis le mois précédent.
J'ai contacté votre service client à deux reprises, par téléphone puis par courriel, sans obtenir de réponse satisfaisante.
Je vous serais donc reconnaissant de bien vouloir vérifier ce dossier et de me communiquer une facture rectifiée dans les meilleurs délais.
Vous trouverez ci-joint une copie du devis ainsi que celle de la facture contestée.
Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je reste à votre disposition pour tout complément d'information.
Je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
Claire Dubreuil
passages.english:
Claire Dubreuil
14 Rue des Lilas, 75011 Paris
Customer Service - Énergie Plus
8 Avenue de la République, 69003 Lyon
Paris, 5 February 2026
Subject: Complaint regarding invoice no. 4521
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to you regarding invoice no. 4521, received on 20 January, whose amount seems incorrect to me.
Indeed, the rate applied does not match the one shown on the quote you sent me the previous month.
I have contacted your customer service twice, by phone and then by email, without receiving a satisfactory response.
I would therefore be grateful if you could check this file and send me a corrected invoice as soon as possible.
You will find enclosed a copy of the quote as well as the disputed invoice.
Awaiting your reply, I remain available for any further information.
Please accept, Sir or Madam, the expression of my distinguished greetings.
Claire Dubreuil

lessons.title: Le compte rendu
lessons.description: Write a clear, organised report of a meeting or event.

blocks.heading: What a compte rendu is for
blocks.body: A compte rendu is a faithful, organised account of what was said and decided at a meeting or event — not a personal opinion piece. It answers: who was there, what was discussed, what was decided, and what happens next. Neutral, factual language matters more than style here.

examples.french: Compte rendu de la réunion du 14 mars
examples.english: Minutes of the meeting of 14 March

examples.french: Étaient présents : cinq membres de l'équipe.
examples.english: Present: five team members.

examples.french: Le point suivant a été abordé :
examples.english: The following item was discussed:

blocks.tip: Write in the passé composé or present for reported facts — avoid the imparfait, which sounds like a story rather than a record.

blocks.heading: Structure of a compte rendu
blocks.body: A clear compte rendu follows the order of the ordre du jour (agenda): a heading with date, attendees and absentees; one paragraph per agenda point, stating what was discussed and what was decided; and a closing section listing follow-up actions and deadlines.

examples.french: 1. Ouverture de la séance
examples.english: 1. Opening of the session

examples.french: Décision : le budget est validé à l'unanimité.
examples.english: Decision: the budget is approved unanimously.
examples.note: decisions stated in bold, simple sentences

examples.french: Actions à suivre : envoyer le devis avant vendredi.
examples.english: Follow-up actions: send the quote before Friday.
examples.note: closing section with responsibilities and deadlines

blocks.heading: Reporting what was said, neutrally
blocks.body: A compte rendu often needs to report other people's statements without quoting them word for word. Reported speech verbs like 'indiquer que', 'préciser que', 'souligner que', and 'proposer de' let you summarise a speaker's point while keeping a neutral, professional distance.

blocks.heading: Reported speech (le discours indirect)
blocks.body: A compte rendu reports what people said without quoting them directly. Direct speech 'Il a dit : « Le budget est trop juste »' becomes indirect: 'Il a indiqué que le budget était trop juste.' The tense shifts back one step (present → imparfait, futur → conditionnel) when the reporting verb is in the past.

examples.french: Elle a dit : « Nous finirons à temps. » → Elle a dit que nous finirions à temps.
examples.english: She said: "We will finish on time." → She said that we would finish on time.

examples.french: Il a précisé que le retard venait du fournisseur.
examples.english: He specified that the delay came from the supplier.
examples.note: imparfait for a reported present-tense fact

examples.french: Le président a annoncé que la réunion suivante aurait lieu en mai.
examples.english: The chair announced that the next meeting would take place in May.
examples.note: futur antérieur becomes conditionnel passé for anterior facts

blocks.tip: Reporting verbs like 'indiquer que', 'préciser que', 'annoncer que' keep the tone neutral — avoid 'il paraît que', which sounds like gossip.

blocks.heading: The passive voice for neutral reporting
blocks.body: A compte rendu often hides who exactly did something, focusing instead on the fact itself. The passive voice ('être' + past participle) and the impersonal 'il a été décidé que' let you report decisions and actions without naming an actor every time.

passages.title: Compte rendu de la réunion d'équipe
passages.french:
Compte rendu de la réunion d'équipe – 14 mars 2026
Étaient présents : Nadia Belkacem, Thomas Girard, Léa Fontaine et Karim Haddad. Sophie Marchand était excusée.
La séance a été ouverte à 9 heures par Nadia Belkacem, qui a présidé la réunion.
Premier point : avancement du projet « Site Vitrine ». Thomas a indiqué que le développement avait pris deux semaines de retard à cause d'un problème technique.
Il a proposé de reporter la mise en ligne au 30 avril, ce que le groupe a approuvé à l'unanimité.
Deuxième point : budget marketing. Léa a présenté un bilan des dépenses du trimestre et a souligné que le budget restait dans les limites prévues.
Une discussion a suivi au sujet de la répartition du budget restant entre publicité en ligne et événements.
Il a été décidé que Karim serait responsable de préparer une proposition détaillée avant la prochaine réunion.
Troisième point : recrutement. Nadia a annoncé qu'un nouveau poste serait ouvert dès le mois de mai.
Actions à suivre : Thomas doit transmettre le nouveau calendrier avant vendredi ; Karim doit finaliser sa proposition budgétaire avant le 25 mars.
La séance a été clôturée à 10 h 15.
Prochaine réunion prévue le 11 avril.
passages.english:
Minutes of the team meeting – 14 March 2026
Present: Nadia Belkacem, Thomas Girard, Léa Fontaine and Karim Haddad. Sophie Marchand was excused.
The session was opened at 9 a.m. by Nadia Belkacem, who chaired the meeting.
First item: progress on the "Showcase Website" project. Thomas indicated that development had fallen two weeks behind due to a technical problem.
He proposed postponing the launch to 30 April, which the group approved unanimously.
Second item: marketing budget. Léa presented a review of the quarter's spending and pointed out that the budget remained within the planned limits.
A discussion followed about splitting the remaining budget between online advertising and events.
It was decided that Karim would be responsible for preparing a detailed proposal before the next meeting.
Third item: recruitment. Nadia announced that a new position would open as early as May.
Follow-up actions: Thomas must forward the new schedule before Friday; Karim must finalise his budget proposal before 25 March.
The session was closed at 10:15 a.m.
Next meeting scheduled for 11 April.

lessons.title: La note de synthèse
lessons.description: Structure a synthesis note that condenses information from a source.

blocks.heading: What a note de synthèse does
blocks.body: A note de synthèse condenses one or several source documents into a short, structured text that a busy reader can absorb quickly. It does not add opinion or new information — it selects, organises and reformulates what is already in the source, keeping only what is essential and relevant.

examples.french: Ce document synthétise les principaux résultats de l'étude.
examples.english: This document synthesises the study's main findings.

examples.french: L'objectif de cette note est de dégager les points clés du rapport.
examples.english: The purpose of this note is to bring out the report's key points.

blocks.tip: A good note de synthèse could stand alone — a reader who never sees the source should still understand the essential message.

blocks.heading: Structuring the synthesis
blocks.body: A synthesis note typically opens with a short introduction stating the source and the problématique (the central question), develops two or three organised parts, each built around one idea supported by facts from the source, and closes with a brief conclusion — never a personal opinion.

examples.french: Ce rapport soulève la problématique suivante : comment concilier croissance et environnement ?
examples.english: This report raises the following question: how can growth and the environment be reconciled?

examples.french: Dans un premier temps, le document analyse les causes économiques.
examples.english: First, the document analyses the economic causes.

examples.french: En définitive, le texte met en évidence trois enjeux majeurs.
examples.english: Ultimately, the text highlights three major issues.

blocks.heading: Selecting and condensing information
blocks.body: The hardest skill in a note de synthèse is hierarchizing: deciding what is essential and what can be dropped. Keep facts, figures, and the source's own logic; cut illustrative anecdotes, repetition, and anything that does not serve the problématique. Reformulate in your own words rather than copying sentences.

examples.french: Il convient de retenir uniquement les éléments pertinents.
examples.english: Only the relevant elements should be retained.

examples.french: L'auteur souligne que la tendance s'accélère depuis 2020.
examples.english: The author points out that the trend has accelerated since 2020.

blocks.heading: The gérondif for concise linking
blocks.body: The gérondif ('en' + present participle) packs two ideas into one economical clause — very useful in a note de synthèse, where space is limited. It can express simultaneity, manner, or cause without a second full clause.

examples.french: En soulignant ce chiffre, l'auteur insiste sur l'urgence de la situation.
examples.english: By highlighting this figure, the author stresses the urgency of the situation.

examples.french: Tout en reconnaissant les progrès, le rapport pointe des limites.
examples.english: While acknowledging the progress, the report points out limitations.

examples.french: En comparant les deux études, on observe des résultats proches.
examples.english: By comparing the two studies, one observes similar results.

blocks.tip: The subject of the gérondif must be the same as the subject of the main clause — otherwise the sentence becomes ambiguous or incorrect.

blocks.heading: Logical connectors for structuring ideas
blocks.body: A note de synthèse relies on precise connectors to make its structure visible at a glance: 'd'une part... d'autre part' to balance two ideas, 'par ailleurs' to add a related point, 'en revanche' to contrast, and 'en définitive' or 'en somme' to conclude.

passages.title: Note de synthèse : le télétravail en France
passages.french:
Ce document propose une synthèse de plusieurs rapports consacrés à l'essor du télétravail en France depuis 2020.
Les sources principales sont une étude du ministère du Travail et une enquête menée auprès de trois cents entreprises.
La problématique centrale est la suivante : le télétravail transforme-t-il durablement l'organisation du travail, ou ne s'agit-il que d'un ajustement temporaire ?
D'une part, les études montrent une hausse constante du nombre de salariés concernés, en particulier dans les grandes entreprises urbaines.
Les employés interrogés soulignent un meilleur équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, ainsi qu'une réduction du temps de transport.
D'autre part, plusieurs rapports mettent en évidence des limites : isolement social, difficulté à séparer travail et repos, et inégalités selon les métiers.
Les cadres et les employés de bureau bénéficient largement du télétravail, tandis que les métiers manuels en restent exclus.
Par ailleurs, certaines entreprises constatent une baisse de la cohésion d'équipe et remettent en question l'efficacité des réunions à distance.
En revanche, d'autres organisations ont adopté un modèle hybride qui semble concilier flexibilité et maintien du lien collectif.
Ce modèle repose généralement sur deux ou trois jours de présence au bureau, réservés aux réunions et au travail collaboratif.
Certains experts recommandent également une formation des managers à l'encadrement à distance.
En définitive, les documents analysés convergent vers une conclusion nuancée : le télétravail s'installe durablement, mais son organisation reste à ajuster.
Les entreprises devront donc structurer des règles claires pour éviter les dérives tout en préservant les bénéfices observés.
passages.english:
This document offers a synthesis of several reports on the rise of teleworking in France since 2020.
The main sources are a study by the Ministry of Labour and a survey conducted among three hundred companies.
The central question is as follows: does teleworking durably transform the organisation of work, or is it merely a temporary adjustment?
On the one hand, studies show a steady rise in the number of employees affected, particularly in large urban companies.
Employees surveyed point to a better balance between professional and personal life, as well as reduced commuting time.
On the other hand, several reports highlight limitations: social isolation, difficulty separating work from rest, and inequalities depending on occupation.
Executives and office employees benefit widely from teleworking, while manual trades remain excluded from it.
Furthermore, some companies note a decline in team cohesion and question the effectiveness of remote meetings.
In contrast, other organisations have adopted a hybrid model that seems to reconcile flexibility with maintaining a collective bond.
This model generally relies on two or three days of office presence, reserved for meetings and collaborative work.
Some experts also recommend training managers in remote management.
Ultimately, the documents analysed converge on a nuanced conclusion: teleworking is settling in for the long term, but its organisation still needs adjusting.
Companies will therefore need to set clear rules to avoid excesses while preserving the observed benefits.

questions.prompt: What is the central question (problématique) of this synthesis?
options: Whether teleworking is a lasting transformation or a temporary adjustment
Whether offices should be closed permanently
Whether commuting time is too long
questions.answer: Whether teleworking is a lasting transformation or a temporary adjustment

questions.prompt: According to the synthesis, manual trades benefit from teleworking as much as office employees.
What do some organisations adopt to balance flexibility with team cohesion?
options: A hybrid model with days in the office
A total ban on remote meetings
questions.answer: A hybrid model with days in the office
